normative_and_architecture_claims.statement: 5G-ATG is treated as a civil-aviation deployment profile of 3GPP 5GS/NR, not as a separate universal protocol.
normative_and_architecture_claims.derivation: The report applies the cited 5GS/NR interfaces to an explicitly synthetic aviation deployment; it does not claim a separate standard.
normative_and_architecture_claims.limitation: The profile is not a real operator or aircraft configuration.

normative_and_architecture_claims.statement: Broadcast and pre-security registration metadata are distinct from post-security user-plane payload protection.
normative_and_architecture_claims.derivation: The model records visible broadcast/initial states before security completion and separately records application payload readability.
normative_and_architecture_claims.limitation: No RF capture or real UE protocol trace is performed.

normative_and_architecture_claims.statement: 5G-AKA, NAS/RRC security and user-plane protection are capabilities whose deployed behavior depends on configuration, implementation and key management.

local_evidence.anchor: This is a digital 5G-ATG architecture and security-state model

normative_and_architecture_claims.derivation: The report explicitly separates standards capabilities from deployment claims and uses synthetic HMAC only as a local policy model.
normative_and_architecture_claims.limitation: The model is not an implementation conformance or cryptographic test.

normative_and_architecture_claims.statement: N3/GTP-U identifiers, DNN, S-NSSAI and QFI are session/routing context and QoS fields, not standalone message-origin credentials.
normative_and_architecture_claims.derivation: The weak router accepts a known DNN while the hardened gateway verifies the active session and QFI binding.
normative_and_architecture_claims.limitation: The packet is a synthetic object, not a real GTP-U datagram.

normative_and_architecture_claims.statement: Dedicated-core physical isolation does not by itself establish OAM authorization or a cabin-to-avionics logical boundary.
normative_and_architecture_claims.derivation: The model intentionally contrasts a trusted management bridge and weak inter-zone router with RBAC, approval and protected-boundary controls.
normative_and_architecture_claims.limitation: The real aircraft network partition and OAM protocol must be verified from its approved architecture and ICD.

normative_and_architecture_claims.statement: Aviation impact severity must be tied to the affected aircraft function and safety assessment, not assigned from a generic IT vulnerability label.
normative_and_architecture_claims.derivation: Each report entry states the aviation asset, precondition and boundary needed before assigning 极高/高/中/低.
normative_and_architecture_claims.limitation: The synthetic model cannot replace FHA, SSA, PSSA or certification-basis evidence.

quantitative_claims.statement: The synthetic configuration uses PLMN 999-99, slice sst=1;sd=ATG001, three DNNs and QFI 9.
Trusted registration completes RRC setup, NAS registration request, 5G-AKA, security mode and user-plane readiness in the model.
The digital interference scenario produces registration_timeout and user_plane_ready=false.
The rogue-cell model exposes pre-security metadata; hardened UE returns rogue_cell_rejected while weak UE returns camped_untrusted_cell, and neither has a ready user plane.
The signaling-storm experiment submits 50 attempts in a 1000 ms window; the weak model allocates 50 contexts while the hardened model allocates 10 and rejects 40.

The telemetry tamper input changes altitude from 30000 ft to 500 ft and airspeed from 440 kt to 80 kt while retaining the original authentication tag; the weak path accepts and the hardened path rejects authentication.
The replay experiment submits the same sequence-3 telemetry at 300 ms and again at 320 ms; the first hardened submission succeeds and the second returns replay.
The cabin session has a synthetic TEID allocated from 0x1000 and QFI 9; forged TEID and QFI values are rejected by separate hardened checks.
The unauthorised OAM request attempts to enable cabin_to_avionics_route and disable slice_isolation; the native bridge accepts it, while hardened authorization rejects it.
The capture model marks broadcast SIB, pre-security registration metadata and N3 outer/TEID metadata visible; application payload is readable without app TLS and not directly readable with app TLS.
The final evidence run records 8 focused 5G-ATG tests and 45 full-repository tests passing.

scenario_conclusions.statement: Dedicated-core physical isolation can be weakened by a trusted OAM/N6 bridge unless logical authorization and protected boundaries are independently enforced.
scenario_conclusions.limitation: Real topology, OAM protocol, roles and aircraft ICD are not present.

scenario_conclusions.statement: DNN/S-NSSAI/TEID/QFI configuration must be bound to the active PDU session and source security zone.
scenario_conclusions.limitation: Synthetic packet objects do not prove a vendor UPF implementation behavior.

scenario_conclusions.statement: High-altitude coverage and mobility require explicit old/new session, sequence and recovery handling; this report marks real handover verification as pending.

evidence.anchor: This is a digital 5G-ATG architecture and security-state model

scenario_conclusions.limitation: No handover, flight-path, Doppler or real coverage experiment is claimed.

scenario_conclusions.statement: Dedicated deployment patch, certificate, configuration and rollback processes are high-value security controls.
scenario_conclusions.limitation: No vendor firmware, certificate authority or CVE-specific reproduction is included.

scenario_conclusions.statement: A rogue-cell state can expose pre-security metadata and cause weak UE camping without establishing a user plane; hardened UE rejects the cell in this model.
scenario_conclusions.limitation: Not a real fake-gNB, RF or identity-capture test.

scenario_conclusions.statement: Uu/RRC/NAS loss can prevent registration and user-plane readiness; the model represents this as digital packet loss.
scenario_conclusions.limitation: No RF power, waveform, propagation, antenna or spectrum measurement.

scenario_conclusions.statement: Unbounded registration state allocation is more exposed to signaling pressure than a rate-limited entry point.
scenario_conclusions.limitation: Context allocation is a deterministic resource model, not AMF/SMF performance data.

scenario_conclusions.statement: A weak trusted-transport path can deliver modified telemetry, while application message authentication blocks the modified payload in the model.
scenario_conclusions.limitation: The HMAC is a synthetic policy instrument and not a certified airborne cryptographic implementation.

scenario_conclusions.statement: A receiver without sequence/freshness state accepts repeated telemetry in the model; the hardened gateway rejects the duplicate.
scenario_conclusions.limitation: Real handover, restart and persistent sequence-state behavior remains a test-bench item.

scenario_conclusions.statement: Forged TEID or QFI is accepted by the weak router but rejected by active-session binding checks.
scenario_conclusions.limitation: No real GTP-U or PFCP socket is opened.

scenario_conclusions.statement: Uu broadcast/initial metadata and N3 outer metadata can remain observable even when application payload protection is enabled; no app TLS leaves payload readable in this model.
scenario_conclusions.limitation: No production capture, RF receiver or transport tap is used.

scenario_conclusions.statement: A cabin-to-avionics write path must not be authorized only by DNN or trusted transport; the hardened boundary rejects the synthetic command before application delivery.
scenario_conclusions.limitation: The downstream command is synthetic and does not represent a real aircraft function.

scenario_conclusions.statement: An OAM bridge that trusts a maintenance jump host can accept a cross-domain route mutation; the hardened controller requires identity/approval and preserves the boundary.
scenario_conclusions.limitation: OAM protocol and vendor implementation are synthetic.

scenario_conclusions.statement: UE credentials, firmware and local bridges are design-review attack surfaces, but this project does not claim a real UE firmware or UICC vulnerability.
scenario_conclusions.limitation: Requires authorized UE security, firmware and key-lifecycle testing.

scenario_conclusions.statement: gNB broadcast, neighbor, N2/N3 and slice configuration are configuration-controlled attack surfaces; this project only verifies synthetic trusted/rogue cell states.
scenario_conclusions.limitation: No real gNB, N2/N3 interoperability or RF coverage test.

scenario_conclusions.statement: A ground application must not trust only source IP, DNN, VLAN, TEID or a dedicated-UPF label; it needs aircraft/session/message and semantic validation.
scenario_conclusions.limitation: The ground application and schema are synthetic.
